system: Stock count reference app, if its server were bound to a network address so a phone can reach it
notes: Author-run example. The app is the forge skill's reference slice (server.py and index.html), read on 2026-10-09 and not changed. Verifications V1 to V10 were run that day on loopback against the unmodified app by verify_stock_count.py; V11 to V13 have not been run.
assumptions: Modelled change: the server listens on the machine's network address so a phone on the same Wi-Fi can open the page. This is not built: server.py binds 127.0.0.1 only, and its README says not to expose it.
The network is a home or workshop Wi-Fi that other people's devices also join. It is not reachable from the internet.
One person uses the app. There are no accounts and no login.
The verifications ran on loopback. The behaviours they test (validation, limits, error answers, how the page shows text) do not depend on the listening address.
out_of_scope: The Wi-Fi router, its password and its firmware.
The host computer's operating system and its other software.
Exposure to the internet. A forwarded port or a tunnel makes this model wrong; it would need redoing.
Physical access to the host computer or the phone.
Language-model cases. The app calls no model.

assets.name: stock sheet
assets.why: Item codes, names, shelves and counts. A wrong or wiped sheet means recounting every shelf, and the list shows what is kept and where.

assets.name: host computer account
assets.why: The server runs as the person who started it and can reach that person's other files.

assets.name: display choices
assets.why: Theme and row spacing only; losing them costs two taps.

assets.name: server log
assets.why: One line per request, shown in the terminal. It is the only record of what was asked, and it includes search text.

actors.name: another device on the same network

zones.name: Phone
zones.trust: The user's own phone and browser. The user trusts it; the server does not, and re-checks everything it sends.

zones.name: Shared Wi-Fi
zones.trust: Not controlled. Any device that joins can send to the server, and may be able to read traffic sent in clear text.

zones.name: Host computer
zones.trust: Controlled by the user. Runs the server and holds the only copy of the data.

elements.name: Stock count page in the phone browser
Page from another website, open in a browser on the Wi-Fi

flows.protocol: HTTP, JSON: create, adjust, remove, search
HTTP: the page itself and JSON answers
HTTP, JSON sent straight to the API
one line per request to stderr

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network sends create, adjust and remove requests straight to the API, and they are carried out as if the user had made them, because no request carries any proof of who sent it.
threats.impact: Counts are changed or the whole stock sheet is removed. The user finds out at the next count, with nothing to restore from.
threats.likelihood: depends on who shares the network; it needs only the address and a browser, and V7 shows the server accepts it today

threats.scenario: A page from another website, open in any browser on the network, sends requests to the API in the background and reads or changes the stock sheet, because the API allows every origin and asks for no credential.
threats.impact: The stock sheet is read or changed by a site the user, or anyone else on the network, merely visited.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network sends a request that triggers a fault in the server code or in Python's http.server, and gains the ability to read or write files as the host computer account.
threats.impact: Everything that account can reach on the host computer, not only the stock sheet.
threats.notes: FACT: the Python documentation for http.server says it is not recommended for production and implements only basic security checks (docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html, read 2026-10-09). No fault of this kind was looked for or found here.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network requests the item list and receives the whole stock sheet, because reading needs no credential.
threats.impact: Anyone on the network learns what is kept and on which shelf.
threats.likelihood: depends on who shares the network; it needs one request, and V7 shows the server answers it today

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network that can observe or redirect Wi-Fi traffic reads the stock sheet in transit, alters requests, or answers in place of the server, because the page and the API use plain HTTP.
threats.impact: The stock sheet is read or changed in transit, and the page cannot tell.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network creates items or opens connections without limit until the data file fills the disk or the stock sheet is too long to load, because nothing limits requests or the number of items.
threats.impact: The stock sheet becomes unusable. Recovery means editing the data file by hand.

threats.scenario: The user deletes the data file by accident, or the disk fails, or T1 happens, and the stock sheet is gone because the SQLite file is its only copy.
threats.impact: Every count is lost and every shelf has to be counted again.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network changes a count in the stock sheet and nothing records which device did it or when, because the log holds only the method and path of each request.
threats.impact: A wrong count cannot be traced to its cause, so it cannot be told apart from a counting mistake.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network puts terminal control characters in a request path, and the server log writes them unchanged to the user's terminal, where they can hide or rewrite earlier lines.
threats.impact: The only record of requests can be made to mislead the person reading it.
threats.notes: FACT: the standard library's own log_message removes control characters from Python 3.12 (same documentation page). server.py replaces it with a raw write, and V10 found the escape byte in the log.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network stores an item in the stock sheet whose name is written as markup, so that when the user opens the page the name runs as script and acts with the user's page.
threats.impact: The attacker's script could change or remove counts whenever the user opens the sheet.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network types SQL fragments or wildcard characters into the search and item fields to read or alter rows of the stock sheet beyond what the request should reach.
threats.impact: Rows are read, changed or removed outside the API's rules.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network sends counts as text, true, fractions or negatives, or fields the API does not know, so that the stock sheet holds a value the page and the rules cannot handle.
threats.impact: A stored value that breaks the sheet for every later request.

threats.scenario: Another device on the same network sends malformed requests and reads the error answers for stack traces, file paths or query text that describe the host computer account's files.
threats.impact: Details that make a later fault in the server easier to use.

mitigations.what: A request body over 64 kB is refused before it is read.
Every query is parameterised, wildcard characters in search text are escaped, and the schema refuses negative counts and duplicate codes.
mitigations.where: server.py, list_items, create_item, adjust_item and SCHEMA

mitigations.what: The page sets every string it shows as text and never assembles markup from it.
Counts must be whole numbers in range; an adjustment below zero is refused in one atomic statement.
Every error answer has one fixed shape and carries no trace, path or query text.
A field the API does not know is refused, not ignored.
NOT BUILT. A secret token sent in a header on every API request, compared in constant time; a request without it gets 401.
mitigations.where: would live in server.py, Handler.route, before any route is chosen

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. Allow the page's own origin only, in place of every origin.
mitigations.where: would replace the wildcard in server.py, Handler.send_json

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. Run the server under its own account that can reach only its own folder, behind a maintained web server.
mitigations.where: host configuration; nothing in the app's folder

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. Serve the page and the API over HTTPS with a certificate the phone trusts.
mitigations.where: host configuration (a reverse proxy); nothing in the app's folder

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. A request limit per client address and a ceiling on the number of items.
mitigations.where: would live in server.py, Handler.route and create_item

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. Remove control characters from the request path before the log line is written.
mitigations.where: server.py, Handler.log_message, which replaces the standard library's scrubbed version with a raw write

mitigations.what: NOT BUILT. A dated copy of the data file taken on a schedule, with one restore tried.
mitigations.where: host configuration; the app's README lists backups as absent

verifications.how: verify_stock_count.py --only V1: a body of 65537 bytes is refused with 413; one of 65536 bytes is stored with 201.
verify_stock_count.py --only V2: searching for a percent sign, an underscore, a quote and a quoted clause each match as plain text; 'bolt' still finds its item.
verify_stock_count.py --only V3: in a headless browser, an item name and a search string written as markup appear character for character and create no element.
verify_stock_count.py --only V4: a count sent as text, true, 3.5 or -1 gets 422 naming qty; 7 is stored; 7 minus 8 gets 409 and the count stays 7; 7 minus 7 gives 0.
verify_stock_count.py --only V5: five malformed or misdirected requests each get the fixed error shape and no trace, path or query text.
verify_stock_count.py --only V6: a create with an extra field gets 422 naming it; the same create without it is stored.
verify_stock_count.py --only V7: a read and a write with no credential must each get 401. Observed: 200 and 201.
verify_stock_count.py --only V8: a request from another origin must get no allow-origin header. Observed: a wildcard on the preflight and on the read.
verify_stock_count.py --only V9: 60 requests one after another must meet at least one 429. Observed: 60 answered 200.
verify_stock_count.py --only V10: a request path holding an escape byte must reach the log without it. Observed: the byte is in the log.
On the host: confirm the server process runs as its own account, then as that account try to list the user's home folder; it must be refused.
From the phone: open the http address and confirm it is refused or redirected; open the https address and confirm the browser shows no certificate warning.
Copy yesterday's backup to a scratch folder, start the server on it, and confirm the item count matches the day it was taken.
